question: Nearly 3 500 motorcyclists die on European roads each year1. This highlights the urgent need for additional measures to be taken to improve the safety of motorcyclists, including by raising vehicle safety standards.

In this context, Article 79 of Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 requires the Commission to consider extending the mandatory installation of anti-lock brake systems (ABS) on category L3e-A1 motorcycles (up to 125 cubic centimetres) and to consider presenting a legislative proposal to that effect2.

A study published in 2020 concluded that ABS should be a requirement for all new motorcycles placed on the European market3 because of the significant role it plays in reducing the frequency and severity of collisions. In addition, ABS systems have been proven to reduce road accident involvement by around 30 %, making a decisive contribution to saving human lives4.

However, six years after the publication of the study in question, the Commission’s planned legislative proposal has not yet been presented. In view of the above, can the Council answer the following: 1.
How does it assess the Commission’s six-year delay in presenting the envisaged legislative proposal, despite clear scientific evidence of the significant benefits of ABS for road safety?

Does it intend to invite the Commission to present a targeted legislative proposal to extend the mandatory installation of ABS to category L3e-A1 motorcycles, irrespective of the broader revision of Regulation (EU) No 168/2013?
